models.description: Fastest catalog pick: Microsoft's 3.8B instruct model at ~2.5 GB—ideal for quick correction and drafting on tight RAM or when you want low latency. Multilingual including English and German; MIT license. Less depth than 8B+ models for long-form or nuanced translation.
models.license_note: MIT — see Microsoft Phi-4 model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: Open-weight reasoning-style model distilled from DeepSeek-R1 into the Qwen-7B architecture: strong math, logic, and step-by-step answers. Replies often include a visible chain-of-thought style trace before the final answer—great for analysis, awkward for polished prose; prefer Ministral 3 or Qwen 3.5 when you want clean copy.
models.license_note: MIT — DeepSeek R1 distill; base Qwen license applies; see Hugging Face model cards.

models.description: Tencent's translation-focused 7B model—strong pick for Translate DE ↔ EN modes when you want a model tuned for multilingual transfer rather than general chat. ~4.7 GB download; pair with Ministral 3 or Qwen 3.5 for correction and open-ended drafting.
models.license_note: Tencent Hunyuan Community License — see Tencent model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: Recommended starting model: Mistral's current 8B instruct checkpoint with crisp answers and reliable EN/DE for drafting and translation-style prompts. Successor to Mistral 7B v0.3 with stronger multilingual support.
models.license_note: Apache-2.0 — see Mistral model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: Efficient 9B instruct with strong multilingual behavior—successor to Qwen 3 8B for everyday correction and translation at ~6 GB. Maguna disables thinking mode and filters reasoning control tokens so replies stay polished.
models.license_note: Apache-2.0 — Qwen3.5; see Alibaba model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: Z.ai's compact 9B instruct checkpoint (April 2025 refresh): strong multilingual chat including English and German at ~6.2 GB. Good everyday alternative to Qwen 3.5 9B when you want GLM-style answers. Maguna uses GLM-4 role-token formatting (`[gMASK]<sop>` layout) and strips control tokens from displayed output.
models.license_note: MIT — see Z.ai / THUDM GLM-4 model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: Google's current mid-size instruct model with clear, safe answers and solid EN/DE quality—good when Qwen 3 14B is too heavy. Replaces Gemma 2 9B with a newer generation at a similar download size (~7 GB). Maguna uses Gemma 4 turn formatting with thinking disabled and filters internal channel tokens from displayed output.
models.license_note: Gemma license — see Google Gemma terms on Hugging Face model card.

models.description: Mid-flagship for careful English and German writing, translation, and proofreading: strong instruction following and long-form consistency. Expect ~9 GB on disk—use Qwen 3.5 9B or Ministral 3 8B if your machine is tighter. Maguna disables thinking mode and filters reasoning control tokens so replies stay polished.
models.license_note: Apache-2.0 — Qwen3; see Alibaba model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: Heavy flagship: Alibaba's latest 27B dense instruct model for maximum EN/DE writing quality when you have the headroom—expect ~16 GB on disk and 32 GB+ system RAM for comfortable use. Maguna disables thinking mode and filters reasoning control tokens; not recommended on laptops with 16 GB RAM.
models.license_note: Apache-2.0 — Qwen3.6; see Alibaba model card on Hugging Face.

models.description: Z.ai's 30B MoE flagship (~3B active per token) for maximum reasoning quality when you have the headroom—expect ~18.5 GB on disk and 24 GB+ system RAM for comfortable use. Maguna disables hybrid thinking (`/nothink`) and filters internal reasoning tokens from displayed output. Heavier than Qwen 3.6 27B; long multi-turn chat may be slower on 16 GB laptops.
models.license_note: MIT — see Z.ai GLM-4.7-Flash model card on Hugging Face.
